nodes.label: Debrief correction
nodes.rationale: A second debrief for the same resource on the same segment in the same OP was stored as another search, so a correction was counted twice (50% then a corrected 30% became 65% under cumulative POD). Recording a debrief when one already exists prompts Replace it / Add as another sortie / Cancel. The check reads the server so it also catches an entry made moments earlier in another window. Replace and Edit overwrite the record in place, keeping its recorded time and attached tracks and setting correctedAt. Delete removes the record; attached track lines stay in the OP DataSync. Treating every debrief as a new sortie was the previous behaviour and was rejected.

nodes.label: POA lock
nodes.rationale: Planning needs a fixed probability of area to build the next period's IAP and priorities while debriefs from the current period keep arriving and may be corrected. Locking is an explicit CASIE action (src/domain/poaLock.ts) for an upcoming OP, stored as op.<n>.poa.<lockedAt>, recording the POA values and a fingerprint of each debrief it was computed from. A lock for OP n uses the Initial Consensus plus every debrief and clue recorded for OPs before n. Corrections remain allowed. When a debrief the lock used is replaced, edited, or deleted, or one of those inputs is added late, or the consensus or segments change, the lock is shown stale and planning decides whether to re-lock. Nothing changes the locked values automatically, because the IAP and assignments built on the lock would change without a decision. Attaching a track, renaming a label, or a correction that keeps the same POD and coverage does not stale the lock. Re-locking writes a new key and earlier locks are kept. Because Mission Properties keep no history (ADR-001), the lock key is the record of what planning used. The UI must show staleness on the POA display and the IAP.

nodes.label: Cumulative POD and POA update
nodes.rationale: After each debrief, segment POA becomes POA times (1 - POD/100), renormalized with the rest of the world. Debriefs on the same segment in the same OP combine as independent searches: cumulative POD = 1 - product of (1 - POD times coverage). Cumulative probability of success compounds across operational periods. A corrected debrief must count once in that rollup.

nodes.label: Block debrief edits after POA lock
nodes.rationale: Would keep a lock from silently disagreeing with the record. Rejected (Paul, 2026-10-11) because a wrong POD would stay in the incident record, or be fixed only by adding another sortie, which double-counts it.

nodes.label: Auto-recompute locked POA
nodes.rationale: Rejected because the IAP and assignments built on the lock would change under planning without a decision being made.
